subtitle: Lesson 95 · Database Design Fundamentals

caption: Guarantees two things at once: every value unique, and never NULL.
Naming it explicitly (PK_Department) gives you something predictable to reference later.

eyebrow: Composite — when one column isn't enough
caption: Neither column alone is unique — but the PAIR always is. Real example: SalesOrderDetail.

code:
-- Default: builds a CLUSTERED index
ALTER TABLE dbo.Department
ADD CONSTRAINT PK_Department PRIMARY KEY (DepartmentID);

-- Explicit override, if something else deserves the clustered slot
PRIMARY KEY NONCLUSTERED (DepartmentID)
caption: A primary key isn't just an identity guarantee — by default, it's your table's physical sort order too.

subtitle: How one table's primary key protects another table's data.
